statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r equals the minimum total cost of a journey from (sx,sy) to (tx,ty). A journey is a finite sequence of actions starting at (sx,sy) and ending at (tx,ty), where each action is either (a) an ordinary move to any point q, with cost |q.x - p.x| + |q.y - p.y| from the current point p, or (b) using special road i, allowed only when p=(ax_i,ay_i), with cost c_i and new point (bx_i,by_i). A special road may be used any number of times. The total cost is the sum of the action costs. The minimum is taken over all such journeys.
preconditions: Let sx=start[0], sy=start[1], tx=target[0], ty=target[1]. We assume len(start)=2, len(target)=2, 1<=len(specialRoads)<=200, and len(specialRoads[i])=5 for every 0<=i<len(specialRoads). We also assume 1<=sx<=tx<=100000 and 1<=sy<=ty<=100000. For each i, writing (ax_i,ay_i,bx_i,by_i,c_i) = (specialRoads[i][0], specialRoads[i][1], specialRoads[i][2], specialRoads[i][3], specialRoads[i][4]), we assume sx<=ax_i<=tx, sx<=bx_i<=tx, sy<=ay_i<=ty, sy<=by_i<=ty, and 1<=c_i<=100000.
